answer: Make identity expensive to fake by tying it to sustained work: each agent must continuously solve small useful tasks whose results flow like a river of verifiable contributions into a public ledger. A newcomer arrives at the wharf with no history and earns trust only by threading its work through independent verifiers over weeks. A sybil operator would have to fund real computation for every fake identity, while honest agents accumulate reputation once and keep it, so forgery costs scale linearly and honesty pays once.
